product: commentary — no product. The unscripted-reaction production rule (founder calls + POV reaction ads).
body: The rule: the reaction cannot be scripted. Founder-customer call format: the founder calls a real customer unannounced and asks why they keep ordering, how long they've used it, whether they see a difference — spontaneous answers are the ad. Scripted dies; people spot fake reactions instantly. Same for POV reaction ads: no face, product filmed from the buyer's POV, live unscripted reaction, minimal text and editing. Rawness is the format, not a budget limitation.
idea: Unscripted reaction is the product — rawness is the format's engine, not its constraint.
sequencing: POV reaction spec (no face, buyer POV, live reaction).
why_it_works: Humans are lie detectors for performed emotion — genuine surprise can't be faked, and messiness reads as truth.
what_to_steal: LC POV unboxing/water-test reactions: no face, buyer's POV, genuine first reaction to the jewelry surviving water — minimal editing.

product: A fitness smartwatch ad experiment (brand unnamed) — first-person vs third-person POV test.
body: An AI Creation Lab experiment: a fitness smartwatch ad with the same character, product, action, and environment — only the POV changed. Same story, different perspective, completely different viewing experience. Asks viewers which feels more immersive. Two 12s videos attached.
cta: "Which POV makes the ad feel more immersive to you, (A)First-person or (B) Third-person?" (engagement).
idea: POV is an independent variable — same ad, two perspectives, different immersion.
sequencing: AI Creation Lab: a POV experiment.
Only the POV changed: first-person vs third-person.
why_it_works: Controlled experiments make the audience co-researchers — engagement plus insight.
what_to_steal: Run the same A/B for LC: first-person wrist POV vs third-person model shot, same piece, measure immersion/CTR.

product: commentary — no product. Hyper-real first-person POV footage technique (polar/iceberg example).
body: Ditching obvious CGI for raw, ultra-realistic visual tension is a conversion unlock; near-100% watch time comes from a narrative hook around a high-stakes real-world perspective triggering vertigo and curiosity. Hook in the first 2 seconds with authentic detail: boots dangling 80ft over a polar ocean, raw wind/creaking audio, iceberg approach through a natural ice arch. Raw gritty realism stops the scroll; drop viewers into real danger and retention follows. 10s video attached; transcript has no speech.
idea: Hyper-real first-person danger POV equals near-100% watch time.
why_it_works: Vertigo triggers a physiological response — the body reacts before the brain can scroll.
what_to_steal: The 2-second authentic-detail recipe for LC: hyper-real first-person macro POV — water beading on the jewelry, the clasp clicking — visceral product truth.
